name: Fig-Draw
description: Browser-based post-processing editor for scientific figures — arrange panels, recolor from a 120-palette library, resize like figsize, and export publication-ready PNG/SVG. Runs entirely client-side.

paragraphs: A browser-based post-processing editor for scientific figures. Bring the SVGs you already exported from Origin, matplotlib, GraphPad Prism, etc. (and raster images like micrographs); SciCompose assembles them into one publication-ready figure — arrange panels, resize like figsize, recolor data series from a 120-palette library, refine single elements, unify type and line weights, and export a submission-grade PNG plus a re-editable SVG.
It runs entirely in your browser — no backend, no accounts, no AI, nothing leaves your machine. It is not a plotting tool; it post-processes figures you already made.
features: SVG figures — fully recognized & editable (axes, ticks, data, scatter, legend, text).
Raster images (PNG/JPG/WebP) — placed as image panels; scale (aspect-locked) and
Model-based resize (figsize) — drag a panel and the axes lengthen/shorten while
font size, line width, marker size, tick length, and label-to-axis distance stay constant, exactly like changing figsize in matplotlib/Origin. Repeated resizes are drift-free and reversible.
120-palette color library, grouped & collapsible: Journal (ggsci — Nature/Science/
